Sam / Priya —

Quick answers inline: 

1) Redis Vector + hot-prefix caching: Yes, we’ve validated p50 ~90-120ms at 256 token average when using prefix/KV caching on queries and a 5k-doc in-memory hot set. Our runbook shows cache warmup steps. If you expect much longer doc lengths we can size accordingly.

2) Rolling delta seeding: absolutely. The partial_backfill_plan.csv uses a daily modified_at window and a backfill watermark to avoid reprocessing duplicates. For heavy update tables we recommend an initial bulk seed for cold docs and then continuous delta ingestion.

3) Rerank metrics: we’ll provide a runnable eval harness (python3) that outputs MRR@5, NDCG@10, Precision@1, and failure rate for regenerations. You can run it locally against your labeled holdout. We’ll also publish a Jupyter with reproducible sampling and seed.

Two operational suggestions unique to this migration:
- Hybrid vectorstore: hot set in managed Redis (SSD-backed) for most recent 100k docs; warm archive in FAISS on object storage for cold items. This keeps p50 low while reducing footprint.
- Canary policy: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if MRR@5 drops > 4 points.

Can Marissa propose 2 possible slots for the runbook walkthrough? I’ll loop Monica for the rerank test plan.

Attachments: polaris_sync_runbook_v1.pdf (attached)

—David

Quick confirmation after internal review:

- Acceptance criteria for the rerank canary:
  * MRR@5 on holdout >= baseline - 2 points (baseline = current Polaris prod ranking)
  * NDCG@10 >= baseline - 3 points
  * No regressions > 1% in Precision@1 for top intent queries
  * End-to-end p50 latency <= 180ms on canary traffic slice

- Plan for backfill:
  * Phase 1 (day 0–2): seed 50k cold docs to staging index (validate schema, tokenization).
  * Phase 2 (day 3–10): continuous delta ingestion with watermarking; nightly integrity checks.
  * Phase 3 (post day 10): full index reconciliation and final sweep (throttled).

- Canary cadence we’ll execute: 5% -> 20% (48h) -> 50% (24h) -> 100% (monitor 72h). Auto-rollback threshold: MRR@5 drop > 4 points or error rate increase > 0.5%.

Operational notes:
- We’ll push a small instrumentation script to your staging cluster to emit token-level cost and latency breakdowns to our console.
- For vector DB choice: managed Redis + FAISS archive is our recommended default; if Polaris chooses single-store we’ll provide sizing guidance.
